thread:
alex: Ran a night run of the 32xTP pipeline with FP8 quant enabled. Aggregate throughput is ~18% lower than the FP16 baseline. nvprof/NCCL timeline shows a spike in all-reduce stalls per step. Posting the short log snippet:

alex: ```
Step 100: compute 42ms | allreduce 18ms | wait 12ms | iter 72ms
FP16 baseline: compute 40ms | allreduce 6ms | iter 58ms
``` 

alex: Also noticed KV cache updates seem to trigger extra cross-rank syncs when sequence length > 1024, not sure if that's the root cause.

sophia: Hmm, 18% is significant. Do you have the NCCL trace? Could be reduced precision causing tensor fragmentation and extra small all-reduces.

alex: Uploaded trace to s3://redwood-perf/traces/1749991234/nccl.html. Key observations: many small allreduces (~120µs each) instead of fewer large ones. The FP8 tensors are split into more segments at the transport layer.

chris: We saw this before when kernel selection didn't fuse quant/dequant for matmul shards. If the runtime emits separate pre/post ops, we get extra buffers and extra collectives.

maria: Also look at our batching heuristic. For mixed seq workloads the packer creates many tiny micro-batches which increases the frequency of KV syncs and reduces overlap opportunities.

sophia: Quick ideas:
- Try enabling NCCL async progress and background thread to overlap comm.
- Switch to fused quant kernels (single fused op for GEMM+quant) to reduce intermediate copies.
- Shard the KV cache by TP rank so updates are local; only metadata needs global sync.

alex: Can someone run a microbench for all-reduce with FP8-shaped tensors? I want raw numbers for different segment sizes.

perf-bot: New perf trace created: s3://redwood-perf/benchmarks/allreduce-fp8/1749991250.json (uploaded by alex). Summary: avg small allreduce 128µs, large allreduce (8MB) 9ms. No alerts.

chris: Quick command we used before:
```bash
python -m perf_tools.allreduce_bench --dtype=fp8 --size=32 --segments=8 --iters=500
```
Expect segment overhead >> consolidated transfer cost. If segments<4, fewer collectives but bigger mem copies.

maria: I'll run the bench on the 32-GPU cluster and also flip the batching packer to prefer larger micro-batches for L>512. Will report numbers.

sophia: Also try layerwise FP8 scaling thresholds. We had a regression when one layer's activations overflowed and the runtime added extra scaling ops per shard.

alex: Good call. That matches a log snippet where we applied an extra scale/unscale around attention keys leading to an extra all-reduce for the scale factors.

maria: Running now. ETA ~15m. Will capture nvprof + NCCL timeline.

alex: If KV cache sharding fixes it, we can disable the global sync path for cache writes and instead have a periodic compaction step.

chris: We should be careful: sharding reduces per-step comm but complicates rollouts and retrievals. Maybe start with read-local, write-shard pattern.

sophia: For the runtime change, we can try two patches:
1) kernel: emit fused GEMM+quant to remove copies
2) comm: aggregate per-step small allreduces into a single batched allreduce per rank when possible
Both are low-risk and can be A/B'd.

perf-bot: Alert: Candidate patch 1749989999-fuse-quant-kernel is in CI and shows ~4% improvement on unit microbench (fp8 matmul). No regressions recorded.

alex: Great. Maria please paste the bench numbers when you have them and include variance.

maria: Bench done. Quick summary:
- baseline FP16: iter 58ms ±2
- FP8 naive: iter 72ms ±4 (allreduce count ~12/step)
- FP8 + fused kernel: iter 66ms ±3
- FP8 + KV-shard + fused: iter 60ms ±2 (allreduce count ~3/step)

maria: nvprof shows overlap improved a lot once we reduced the collective count. Uploading traces to s3.

alex: This is promising — KV-shard + fused kernels almost recovers baseline. Next steps: safety tests on retrieval correctness, update rollout plan, and a small canary on dedicated cluster.

sophia: I'll open a PR for fused kernel and a toggle for KV-shard with feature flag. Mentioned perf numbers in the PR description.

chris: Also add a microbench to CI that measures allreduce count per step for quantized config.

alex: Thanks all. If anyone else sees similar regressions on other clusters please post here. :thumbsup!

maria: noted. I'll coordinate the canary and post results in this thread.
